quickSummary: Equilibrium constant K is thermodynamically linked to free energy by Δ_r G° = -RT ln K. The van 't Hoff equation governs temperature dependence: heating increases K for endothermic reactions (ΔH > 0) and decreases K for exothermic reactions (ΔH < 0).
summary: Master standard free energy relations, equilibrium constant magnitude criteria, and van 't Hoff temperature shifts.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.1 Thermodynamics of Equilibrium (Δ_r G°)
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.1 Thermodynamics of Equilibrium (Δ_r G°)

summaryBox.title: Free Energy & Equilibrium
summaryBox.takeaway: Δ_r G° = -RT ln K. If Δ_r G° < 0 ⟹ K > 1 (Products favored). If Δ_r G° > 0 ⟹ K < 1 (Reactants favored).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
THERMODYNAMIC POSITION OF EQUILIBRIUM
                      
   If Δ_r G° < 0 ⟹ K > 1:  Products favored at equilibrium (Exergonic).
   If Δ_r G° = 0 ⟹ K = 1:  Reactants and Products present in equal proportions.
   If Δ_r G° > 0 ⟹ K < 1:  Reactants favored at equilibrium (Endergonic).
conceptBreakdown.content:
The standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta_r G^\circ$) dictates the thermodynamic position of equilibrium:
$$\Delta_r G = \Delta_r G^\circ + RT \ln Q$$
At equilibrium, $\Delta_r G = 0$ and the reaction quotient $Q = K_{\text{eq}}$:
$$\mathbf{\Delta_r G^\circ = -RT \ln K = -2.303 RT \log_{10} K} \quad \implies \quad \mathbf{K = e^{-\Delta_r G^\circ / RT}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.2 The van 't Hoff Equation (Temperature Dependence of K)
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.2 The van 't Hoff Equation (Temperature Dependence of K)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
TEMPERATURE SHIFT MECHANICS
                       
   ENDOTHERMIC REACTION (Δ_r H° > 0):  T₂ > T₁ ⟹ K₂ > K₁ (K increases as T rises).
   EXOTHERMIC REACTION  (Δ_r H° < 0):  T₂ > T₁ ⟹ K₂ < K₁ (K decreases as T rises).
conceptBreakdown.content:
The equilibrium constant $K$ is independent of initial concentrations, pressure, volume, or catalysts, and varies STRICTLY with Temperature ($T$):
$$\frac{d \ln K}{dT} = \frac{\Delta_r H^\circ}{R T^2}$$
Integrating from $T_1$ to $T_2$ assuming constant reaction enthalpy $\Delta_r H^\circ$:
$$\mathbf{\ln \left( \frac{K_2}{K_1} \right) = \frac{\Delta_r H^\circ}{R} \left( \frac{1}{T_1} - \frac{1}{T_2} \right) = \frac{\Delta_r H^\circ}{R} \left( \frac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2} \right)}$$
$$\mathbf{\log_{10} \left( \frac{K_2}{K_1} \right) = \frac{\Delta_r H^\circ}{2.303 R} \left( \frac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2} \right)}$$

quickRevision: K > 1 when Δ_r G° < 0; K < 1 when Δ_r G° > 0.
van 't Hoff equation: log₁₀(K₂/K₁) = (Δ_r H° / 2.303R) [(T₂ - T₁) / (T₁ T₂)].
keyFormulae: log₁₀(K₂ / K₁) = (Δ_r H° / 2.303 R) [ (T₂ - T₁) / (T₁ T₂) ]
